findings.highlight: I’m skipping school, so I should acquaint my body with fighting as much as time allows.
findings.evidenceJa: 学校を休んでいるんだから、時間の許す限り戦いに体を慣らしておかなければ。
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese ends after Shirou proposes resuming the sparring; this training rationale is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon conditionally restores obsolete source prose and changes what the active scene states.

findings.evidenceJa: 今の俺はほっとけば治るんだから
findings.governingReading: Shirou says the bruising will heal if simply left alone.
findings.explanation: Automatic healing invents a special mechanism where the line asserts ordinary unattended recovery.

findings.evidenceJa: シロウの腕前を知られるのはよくありませんね
findings.governingReading: Saber says it would be bad for the eventual enemy Rin to learn Shirou’s fighting ability or level of skill.
findings.explanation: Powers broadens the tactical object into Shirou’s abilities in general and obscures Saber’s combat assessment.

findings.governingReading: The dojo rings with an anticlimactic, silly sound: Saber’s stomach growling.
findings.explanation: Strange removes the comic evaluation that makes the dignified training scene collapse into hunger.

findings.highlight: They’re coming from the shopping district that Sakura and I go to regularly.
findings.evidenceJa: 奥さんたちが歩いてくる深山町の中心が、俺や桜が愛用しているご近所の商店街である。
findings.governingReading: The neighborhood shopping street Shirou and Sakura frequent is identified as the center of Miyama Town.
findings.explanation: The English omits the location’s relation to Miyama and weakens the work’s concrete urban geography.

findings.governingReading: Shirou pushes the groceries into the bicycle’s basket.
findings.explanation: A basket attached to the bicycle becomes a cart, changing the concrete object and staging.

findings.evidenceJa: むー、と不満そうに口をとがらす。
findings.governingReading: Illya makes a dissatisfied “muu” and sticks out/purses her lips in a pout.
findings.explanation: The generic frown removes the conspicuously childlike vocal and facial gesture that motivates Shirou’s next observation.

findings.highlight: My body unintentionally moves and lowers its waist down so it can move more freely.
findings.evidenceJa: 思わず体が反応して、いつでも動けるように腰を落とした。
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s body reacts reflexively and he lowers his stance so he can move at any moment.
findings.explanation: The English is malformed and replaces a ready combat stance with vague bodily movement.

findings.highlight: The girl clings to my arm as naturally as if she were holding her father’s.
findings.evidenceJa: 父親の手をとるような自然さで俺の腕に抱きついてきた。
findings.governingReading: The girl clings to Shirou’s arm with the natural ease of taking her father’s hand.
findings.explanation: The dangling possessive leaves the concrete hand image incomplete and weakens the paternal intimacy that echoes through the scene.

findings.evidenceJa: フツウの子供って、仲良くお話しするものなんでしょ？
findings.governingReading: Illya asks whether ordinary children are supposed to talk together on friendly terms.
findings.explanation: The ungrammatical English blurs both the act of friendly conversation and her revealing distance from ordinary childhood.

findings.highlight: As I tried to make her let go, the girl almost falls to the ground.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺に振り払われた反動で、少女は背中から地面に倒れそうになる。
findings.governingReading: The force of Shirou shaking her off sends Illya toward a backward fall, back-first onto the ground.
findings.explanation: Tried weakens the completed cause and the English omits the direction of the fall, making the rescue staging less precise.

findings.highlight: When I notice, I instantly reached out for Illyasviel
findings.evidenceJa: 気が付けば、俺は咄嗟にイリヤスフィール
findings.governingReading: By the time Shirou realizes it, he has reflexively reached for Illya and caught her.
findings.explanation: The tense sequence is ungrammatical and obscures the involuntary speed of Shirou’s protective response.

findings.evidenceJa: とんでもないアンバランスさだ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou reacts to the extraordinary mismatch between Illya’s lethal threat and her absolute, childlike trust.
findings.explanation: Unbalanced reads as a judgment that Illya is mentally unstable rather than a description of the scene’s startling contrast.

findings.highlight: But I think I got a lot of things as good as that.
findings.evidenceJa: けどそれに負けないぐらい多くの物をもらってきたと思う
findings.governingReading: Although Shirou inherited no physical traits, he believes he received just as many other things from his father.
findings.explanation: The English turns a comparison of abundance into the malformed claim that the things were “as good,” changing the basis of comparison.

findings.highlight: Illya looks up at me timidly.
findings.evidenceJa: おずおずとこちらを見上げるイリヤ。
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese contains only Illya’s hesitant question; the narration describing a timid upward look is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon conditionally restores obsolete source prose and supplies a physical-emotional cue absent from the active witness.

findings.highlight: the Japanese snack that I’m sure she’s never seen before
findings.evidenceJa: 初めて見るであろう東洋の和菓子
findings.governingReading: Shirou infers that the Eastern sweet is probably something Illya is seeing for the first time.
findings.explanation: I’m sure promotes his likely inference into explicit certainty.

findings.highlight: endure the shock that attacked the back of my head
findings.evidenceJa: 後頭部を襲ったショックに耐える
findings.governingReading: Shirou endures a figurative jolt at the back of his mind/head as he realizes he would like a younger sister like her.
findings.explanation: The Japanese-shaped wording sounds like a literal physical attack and obscures the comic emotional shock.

findings.highlight: she’s a magus by nature from the core.
findings.evidenceJa: その芯は根っからの魔術師だ。
findings.governingReading: Whatever Rin is like outwardly, at her core she is a magus through and through.
findings.explanation: The doubled, malformed construction fails to express the contrast between her surface manner and ingrained magus nature.

findings.highlight: I don’t think Illya is a girl that would want to kill others.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分から人を殺すような子じゃないと思う。
findings.governingReading: From their short exchange, Shirou thinks Illya is not the sort to kill someone on her own initiative.
findings.explanation: Want adds an unsupported claim about desire and weakens the distinction between initiating an act and understanding its meaning.
